name: Distorted Video Volumes (Horseshoe Mapping)
definition: Rendering technique using backward-mapping to distort volume geometry (e.g., into a horseshoe shape) by distorting texture coordinates instead of geometry, allowing planar view-aligned slices to be rendered with modified 3D texture coordinates.
summary: Distorted Video Volumes, or Horseshoe Mapping, renders deformed video data by distorting texture coordinates via inverse mapping in the fragment shader, avoiding the gaps and overlaps inherent in forward geometry deformation.
